headline: High: Pipecat’s shared-bus, multi-API defaults can feed Social Auto Upload with unverified content, creating prompt-injection and cascading-action risk; data leakage is lower because the uploader cannot read files.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Pipecat’s shared bus and stdin/stdout surfaces can carry attacker-controlled text, and social-auto-upload consumes media/account workflows that may act on upstream content. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so prompt-like content from pipecat can plausibly influence downstream automation. This is less than high because direct raw-instruction parsing is not explicitly documented for either agent.
conditions: IF Pipecat output is forwarded into social-auto-upload prompts or captions without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF the two agents share a bus or pipe carrying free-form text, attacker-controlled instructions can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Add a fixed prompt/template wrapper around all Pipecat text before passing it onward.
Strip or escape markdown, URLs, and imperative phrases from upstream text.
Insert a human approval step for any caption or post text derived from Pipecat.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and reject untrusted instruction-like spans.
requires-engineering: separate the agents onto isolated queues with schema validation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Pipecat touches audio, video, images, text, and conversation state, while social-auto-upload does not have filesystem read access and only requests account_name. That makes broad workspace leakage unlikely in the default pair. Residual risk remains if operators manually copy sensitive media or transcripts into the uploader, but the profiles do not show an automatic shared filesystem path.
conditions: IF operators manually paste transcripts or media from Pipecat into social-auto-upload, those contents can leak into uploads.
IF a shared external workspace is introduced outside the profiles, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Keep Pipecat outputs in a separate directory from upload staging.
Avoid placing transcripts or raw audio in files that social-auto-upload can access.
Use redacted media/captions for uploads.
requires-engineering: add access controls or per-agent workspaces.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP checks before upload.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Pipecat has shared-bus concurrency and broad network egress, while social-auto-upload has broad network egress but no filesystem write, shell, or git modification. Their write surfaces do not overlap in the profiles, so direct resource contention is limited. The main conflict is coordination on shared network-dependent workflows, which is usually manageable.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same remote account or API quota, they can contend for rate limits.
IF Pipecat and social-auto-upload share a mutable external resource, race conditions may occur.
mitigations: Stagger network-heavy jobs to avoid quota collisions.
Use separate API credentials per agent.
Monitor for 429/rate-limit responses.
requires-engineering: add distributed locking around shared remote resources.
requires-engineering: implement idempotent retries with conflict detection.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Pipecat can generate text from audio/video inputs, and social-auto-upload can turn that content into published social-media actions. If B treats A’s output as authoritative, a transcription or caption error can cascade into an incorrect post. This is not high because the profiles do not show fully autonomous irreversible actions beyond posting workflows, but the default pipeline is still vulnerable.
conditions: IF social-auto-upload posts captions or descriptions derived from Pipecat without verification, transcription errors can be published.
IF Pipecat outputs are used as the sole source for upload metadata, downstream mistakes cascade.
mitigations: Require a preview/approval step before posting.
Compare Pipecat transcripts against source media for a quick spot-check.
Limit automation to draft creation, not direct publish.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before auto-posting.
requires-engineering: log and diff upstream text against final post text.

E_compliance.rationale: Pipecat’s docs show broad third-party API integrations and analytics/metrics, while social-auto-upload handles account data and uploads to social platforms. The profiles do not specify residency, certifications, or retention mismatches, so only a modest compliance concern is supportable. I cite both because the risk arises from their combined handling of user media and account data, but the evidence is indirect.
conditions: IF regulated media or personal data is routed through third-party APIs in Pipecat and then uploaded by social-auto-upload, policy review is needed.
IF retention or deletion requirements differ between the two services, compliance gaps can appear.
mitigations: Document the data flow for media and transcripts.
Avoid sending regulated data to third-party APIs unless approved.
Set a short manual retention window for staging files.
requires-engineering: add retention/deletion automation.
requires-engineering: map each API to a residency and DPA review.
